_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Burkina Faso covering Mossi Kingdoms, French Upper Volta, Sankara revolution, and contemporary jihadist crisis.

ethnic_groups.name: Mossi
ethnic_groups.notes: Dominant ethnic group; centralised kingdoms (Ouagadougou, Yatenga, Tenkodogo); Mogho Naba paramount chief; Mooré language

ethnic_groups.name: Fulani/Peul
ethnic_groups.notes: Pastoralists across the Sahel zone; Fulfulde language; caught between jihadist recruitment and state suspicion

ethnic_groups.name: Bobo
ethnic_groups.notes: Western Burkina Faso around Bobo-Dioulasso; farming people; traditional festivals

ethnic_groups.name: Gurunsi
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border with Ghana; includes Kassena, Nankana, and Lela subgroups; distinctive painted houses

ethnic_groups.name: Gurma/Gourmantché
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern Burkina; related to kingdom of Fada N'Gourma

ethnic_groups.name: Senufo
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern region; related to Senufo in Côte d'Ivoire and Mali

ethnic_groups.name: Lobi
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Burkina; acephalous society; earth-shrine governance; distinctive terracotta sculpture

ethnic_groups.name: Mande/Dioula
ethnic_groups.notes: Trading communities, especially in Bobo-Dioulasso; linked to West African Mande diaspora

ethnic_groups.name: Tuareg
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Sahel; nomadic Berber pastoralists; Tamashek language

ethnic_groups.name: Dagara
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwestern Burkina; farming people straddling Ghana border

independence.notes: As Upper Volta; renamed Burkina Faso 1984

natural_resources.notes: Africa's fastest-growing gold producer (4th in Africa); artisanal mining (orpaillage) employs ~1M; cotton 'white gold' second export; manganese reserves significant; no oil/gas

military.notes: Two coups in 2022 (Damiba Jan, Traoré Sep); junta expelled French troops (Operation Sabre); now aligned with Russia/Wagner Group; fighting jihadist insurgency (JNIM/ISGS) since 2015; Volunteers for Defense of the Fatherland (VDP) militia; left ECOWAS 2024

debt_aid.notes: Heavily aid-dependent; junta's pivot to Russia complicated Western aid flows; HIPC debt relief beneficiary; cotton subsidies by rich countries harm Burkinabè farmers

top_universities: University of Ouagadougou (now Joseph Ki-Zerbo University)
education.notes: Low literacy (46%); Thomas Sankara's literacy campaigns (1983-87) achieved significant gains; jihadist attacks closing schools in north; French-language instruction; significant gender gap

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 1.5 million (Côte d'Ivoire primary, also Italy, France)
diaspora_migration.notes: Massive seasonal/permanent migration to Côte d'Ivoire (cocoa/coffee plantations); 2002 Ivorian crisis displaced hundreds of thousands of Burkinabè; internally displaced ~2M due to jihadist insurgency

digital_economy.notes: Limited digital infrastructure; FESPACO (Pan-African Film Festival) showcases creative digital economy; mobile money primary financial inclusion tool; conflict disrupting connectivity in north

current_leader.name: Ibrahim Traoré
current_leader.title: President of the Transition
current_leader.notes: Captain who seized power in September 2022 counter-coup; youngest head of state in Africa

former_leaders.name: Maurice Yaméogo
former_leaders.notes: First president of Upper Volta; overthrown by military

former_leaders.name: Sangoulé Lamizana
former_leaders.notes: Military ruler; alternated between military and civilian governance

former_leaders.name: Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo
former_leaders.notes: Military head of state; Sankara was his PM

former_leaders.name: Thomas Sankara
former_leaders.notes: Revolutionary pan-Africanist; renamed country Burkina Faso; assassinated

former_leaders.name: Blaise Compaoré
former_leaders.notes: 27-year rule; overthrew and killed Sankara; ousted by popular uprising 2014

former_leaders.name: Michel Kafando
former_leaders.notes: Transitional president; survived RSP coup attempt

former_leaders.name: Roch Marc Christian Kaboré
former_leaders.notes: Elected president; overthrown amid security crisis

former_leaders.name: Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba
former_leaders.notes: Military coup leader; himself overthrown by Traoré

910.name: Prehistoric Burkina Faso
910.description: Stone Age settlement; Saharan desiccation driving migration southward; early iron-smelting at Kaya.

sub_clusters.name: Neolithic Sahel Transition
sub_clusters.description: Green Sahara to savanna; hunter-gatherer to pastoralist transition.

sub_clusters.name: Early Iron Smelting
sub_clusters.description: Among the earliest iron-smelting sites in West Africa at Kaya and Bura.

920.name: Mossi Kingdoms
920.description: Foundation and consolidation of the Mossi states; resistance to Islamic jihad empires.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Ouagadougou (Wogodogo)
sub_clusters.description: Mogho Naba dynasty; centralised Mossi statecraft; Tenkodogo origins.

sub_clusters.name: Kingdom of Yatenga
sub_clusters.description: Northern Mossi kingdom centred on Ouahigouya; rivalry with Ouagadougou.

sub_clusters.name: Mossi Resistance to Mali and Songhai
sub_clusters.description: Mossi cavalry raids on Timbuktu and Djenné; resistance to Islamic expansion.

920.name: Gurma, Lobi, and Bobo Peoples
920.description: Non-Mossi polities in the east and southwest; acephalous societies; Gurma kingdom.

sub_clusters.name: Gurma Kingdom (Fada N'Gourma)
sub_clusters.description: Eastern kingdom related to Mossi dynasties; buffer between Mossi and Hausa states.

sub_clusters.name: Lobi and Bobo Acephalous Societies
sub_clusters.description: Decentralised southwestern peoples; iron-working; earth-shrine governance.

930.name: Trans-Saharan and Regional Trade Networks
930.description: Long-distance trade through the Mossi plateau; kola, gold, salt, and slave routes.

sub_clusters.name: Mossi Trade Routes
sub_clusters.description: Ouagadougou as trade crossroads; Yarse Muslim trading community; Mossi-Hausa commerce.

sub_clusters.name: Fulani Jihad Impact
sub_clusters.description: Pressure from Macina and Sokoto jihads; Fulani communities in Mossi territory.

940.name: French Conquest and Upper Volta Colony
940.description: French military conquest; Upper Volta colony created, dissolved, recreated; forced labour for coastal colonies.

sub_clusters.name: French Conquest of Mossi Kingdoms
sub_clusters.description: Voulet-Chanoine expedition; sack of Ouagadougou 1896; Mossi capitulation.

sub_clusters.name: Upper Volta Colony
sub_clusters.description: Colony created 1919; dismembered 1932 for forced labour supply; reconstituted 1947.

sub_clusters.name: Forced Labour and Conscription
sub_clusters.description: Voltaic labourers conscripted for Côte d'Ivoire cocoa/coffee plantations and railway construction.

950.name: Postcolonial Upper Volta
950.description: Independence under Maurice Yaméogo; military coups; Lamizana era.

sub_clusters.name: Yaméogo and First Republic
sub_clusters.description: Independence 1 August 1960; single-party rule; trade union opposition; overthrown.

sub_clusters.name: Lamizana Military Rule
sub_clusters.description: Sangoulé Lamizana alternates between military and civilian governance; economic stagnation.

950.name: Thomas Sankara Revolution
950.description: Pan-Africanist revolutionary leader; renamed country Burkina Faso; radical social reforms; assassination.

sub_clusters.name: Sankara Revolutionary Programme
sub_clusters.description: Land reform; mass vaccination; women's rights; anti-corruption; renamed Burkina Faso 1984.

sub_clusters.name: Assassination of Sankara
sub_clusters.description: Blaise Compaoré coup; Sankara killed 15 October 1987; revolution ends.

960.name: Compaoré Era
960.description: Blaise Compaoré's 27-year rule; structural adjustment; regional mediator; popular uprising.

sub_clusters.name: Compaoré Authoritarian Rule
sub_clusters.description: Façade democracy; Norbert Zongo assassination 1998; regional diplomacy.

sub_clusters.name: 2014 Popular Uprising
sub_clusters.description: Mass protests against constitutional amendment; Compaoré flees to Côte d'Ivoire.

960.name: Jihadist Insurgency and Military Coups
960.description: Sahel jihadist expansion; JNIM and ISGS attacks; two military coups 2022; Traoré junta.

sub_clusters.name: Jihadist Expansion
sub_clusters.description: JNIM and ISGS spread from Mali; attacks in Sahel and Est regions; mass displacement.

sub_clusters.name: 2022 Military Coups
sub_clusters.description: Damiba coup January 2022; Traoré coup September 2022; pivot toward Russia/Wagner.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
